subject: Banking
title: Market Making Explained
description: A quick win: understand Market Making Explained.

hook.text: When you buy a stock, a market maker often sells it to you from its own inventory.

buildup.text: Market makers post bid and ask prices. The spread between them, often pennies per share, is their profit.

discovery.text: Without market makers, finding a buyer or seller would take time.

twist.text: Market makers can lose money in volatile markets when prices move against their inventory before they can adjust.

climax.text: Market making is the utility function of finance. It keeps markets liquid so everyone can trade when they want.

punchline.text: Pennies per share, millions of shares. Market makers enable instant trades.

quiz.question: How do market makers earn money?
options: The bid-ask spread on each share they buy and sell
